chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from some of his men, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Every adult, male or female, who falsely accuses a minor or an adult, a male or a female, a Muslim or a disbeliever, a free person or a slave, is subject to the hadd of false accusation; and upon the non-adult is the disciplinary punishment.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What this report contains regarding the obligation of the hadd upon one who accuses a child is to be understood as referring to accusing him by attributing zina to one of his parents, such as saying, “O son of the fornicator,” or “of the fornicatress,” or “Your mother committed zina with you,” or “your father,” because that makes the hadd fully obligatory upon him. But if he says to him, “You have committed zina,” then the hadd is not obligatory upon him, according to what we have previously presented from the reports. As for what it contains regarding the obligation of the hadd upon one who accuses a disbeliever, or a Jew, or a Christian, it is possible that what is meant is when his mother is Muslim; then the hadd is obligatory upon the one who accuses him, due to the sanctity of the Muslim woman. But if that is not the case, then ta'zir is obligatory upon him, according to what we have previously presented.

key_terms.التَّعْزِيرُ: discretionary disciplinary punishment imposed below the level of hadd
key_terms.الزِّنَى: illicit sexual intercourse, the accusation of which triggers qadhf-related rulings
key_terms.بَالِغٍ: a legally mature person subject to full legal responsibility
key_terms.حَدُّ الْفِرْيَةِ: the prescribed legal punishment for false accusation
key_terms.غَيْرِ الْبَالِغِ: one who has not reached legal maturity
key_terms.مُسْلِمَةً: a Muslim woman, whose sanctity is legally protected in this context

ai.seo_question: When does the hadd of false accusation apply in cases involving minors or non-Muslims in Shi'i fiqh?
ai.summary: This report gives a legal ruling concerning false accusation and states that an adult who makes such an accusation is liable for the hadd of defamation, while a non-adult receives disciplinary punishment. The compiler then clarifies that some applications of the report are restricted, especially in cases involving minors or non-Muslims, where the exact wording of the accusation and the honor of a Muslim parent affect whether hadd or ta'zir applies.
